title: Distribution and install - bwrk as a package with scoped install tiers
description: EPIC BRIEF. Make bwrk installable as a normal package with three composable scopes, serving every consumer of the app - not just the global manager (this epic was extracted from the global-manager epic bw_work_855968120dba50c0 for exactly that reason). Tier 1 repo-scoped: bwrk as a dev dependency invoked via pnpm bwrk or npx, nothing on the machine PATH, version pinned in the lockfile so every teammate and CI run uses the same bwrk against the shared .boreal state - per-repo version pinning is a correctness feature for a tool whose value is deterministic records, not a convenience. Tier 2 machine-scoped: npm global or Homebrew putting bwrk on PATH, enabling capture-anywhere and the global manager addon. Tier 3, the global manager itself, is not an install artifact - it is a first-run experience (bwrk global init) owned by the global-manager epic. The mechanism that makes tiers compose instead of conflict: the machine binary DELEGATES to the repo-pinned version when run inside a repo that has one (the Gradle-wrapper and yarn pattern) - the machine binary is a launcher inside repos, the pinned version is what touches repo state, so version skew between teammates cannot produce schema-drifted records; the fail-closed state schemaVersion check remains the backstop. bwrk --version reports both identities (for example 1.4.0 brew delegated to 1.2.3 repo-pinned), doctor warns on skew with channel-correct upgrade advice, and --no-delegate is the debugging escape hatch. install.sh flows: default machine flow (binary, then global-addon prompt only when no registry exists, then offer to link the cwd repo); --repo adds the dev dependency and verifies pnpm bwrk with no PATH changes and no global prompt, auto-linking only when a machine registry already exists (--no-link to skip); --machine installs the binary and skips all global prompts; --global --no-global --yes for non-interactive; idempotent re-runs never re-prompt for what exists and --repo on an installed repo is an upgrade. Accepted trade-off recorded here: delegation adds a startup hop and launcher complexity; the alternative is version-skew bugs in shared state, which are the expensive kind. If delegation must be deferred, the interim floor is a hard doctor error on version mismatch against a repo-pinned version - never silent skew.
acceptanceCriteria: A repo with only the dev-dependency install runs pnpm bwrk end to end with no machine binary present
A machine binary inside a repo-pinned project delegates - bwrk --version shows both identities and repo state is only ever touched by the pinned version, covered by tests
install.sh matrix passes: default, --repo, --machine, and non-interactive flags, idempotent on re-run
npm pack installs globally and brew formula builds from the packed tarball
